goal.summary: MPI-877 is CLOSED - round 3 green on both faults. The conversation that followed found three more causes behind the poor result, none of them MPI-877's: the mask was being forced, the worked example in the system prompt was the prompt that FAILED, and the fix Fabio reached for (composite) is unreachable. The first two shipped as MPI-888. The third is MPI-887, which another session picked up the moment it was carded. completed: MPI-877 CLOSED (done / complete), its 8 file claims released. Fabio's round-3 live run was green on both of its faults: the latents drew in the correct workspace and made an entry on the card, and the prompt named nothing outside the mask ('Convert the boy into a demon: glowing red eyes, sharp horns, pale grey skin, a sinister grin'). The verdict is written into its validation.md under '# Round 3 - Fabio's verdict'.

MPI-888 BUILT AND COMMITTED (7289ee58), card in doing / validating. A new Route rule above the Masking rule: one question - does the request name a PART of the picture? - with three answers. No part named runs whole-picture unasked; a part named with words protecting the rest is a mask already chosen; only a part named with no such words is the user's to decide, and that is the case that was being decided for them. Three bounds stop it becoming a menu: at most three routes, only at a genuine fork, always recommend one. The Masking rule now starts AFTER that fork instead of declaring it.

MPI-888's second half, and it was my bug from last session: the worked example in the system prompt WAS the prompt that failed. I wrote it as the prompt the model 'needed' and never rendered it. Fabio rendered both - the adjective list replaced the boy instead of transforming him and the likeness went with it, while the plain 'convert the boy into a demon version of himself' kept more. The long one stays as the counter-example. Shape stated so it generalises: a VERB and a TARGET, details only when the user named them. Plus a fallback ladder: a bad result moves to a different op or a simpler prompt, never more adjectives - inpaint beat kleinEdit on the picture kleinEdit was the obvious choice for.

MPI-888 evidence, each fix backed out ON ITS OWN: no Route rule -> 2 fail (the Route test and the ladder test, because the ladder lives inside the Route rule - correct, not collateral); the old example restored -> 1 fail, the example test; no ladder -> 1 fail, the ladder test; control -> 0. npm test 1765 tests, 1763 pass, 0 fail, 1 todo (the pre-existing MPI-867 entry). Both lints exit 0. docs/agent/masking.md carries all of it too - the doc is fetched in the asking turn, the system prompt binds in the composing one, which is the lesson MPI-877 paid for.

MPI-887 CARDED (Composite's slot only takes an entry already in the open card's history, MpiToolOptionsComposite.js:16, so an edit that landed as its own card can never be composited with the original). ANOTHER SESSION OWNS IT NOW - it is in doing with its own checklist and files.json, editing routes/projects.js, MpiMediaPicker and MpiPromptBox. I briefly moved it back to todo thinking it was unstarted, and put it back. Do not touch its card or its files.

MPI-889 UMBRELLA opened with three members (f5a72aab), Fabio's three asks from the end of the conversation: MPI-890 the agent reads the open workspace, MPI-891 it moves the view to where its work renders, MPI-892 it fills a Flow and hands it over. Phase order 1->2->3 and it is a HARD ordering, reasoned in tasks/MPI-889/plan.md. He asked for the umbrella explicitly so a handoff keeps working one card instead of three.

The question MPI-877 carried unanswered for three rounds is ANSWERED, by MPI-892's shape. Should the agent RUN detail and inpaint, or teach the user to run them? Neither: FILL AND HAND OVER. The agent fills what it can, opens the surface, and the user corrects the knobs it cannot see before the GPU spends. Fabio arrived at it through Flows; it covers detail and inpaint for the same reason.

MPI-889's members are all `todo` and unstarted. Start at MPI-890: it is the prerequisite for both others and the cheapest of the three - agentService.js:105 already posts `pinned` every turn as renderer UI state, and the workspace is one more key on that same payload, plus a clause in _appStateLine (agentLoop.mjs:747) and one in the Cards rule (agentLoop.mjs:1184).

SETTLE BEFORE PHASE 3, and it is one read: the Duration rule (agentLoop.mjs:1166) says the agent never speaks first and a late generation only reaches it when the user writes again, while the auto-look on settle (agentLoop.mjs:1445) pushes a '[You looked at it: ...]' note and calls _maybeDrained(), whose comment describes a WAKE TURN that reports it. One is stale. The answer also gates the result-review rule below.

THE RESULT-REVIEW RULE is fully specified and NOT built, because it is blocked twice. Fabio's shape: the agent judges its own result, names what broke, and offers the fix. Three entry points, and only one needs it to see anything - (a) structural: a whole-image edit ran and the user only wanted part changed, so composite is on the table whether or not damage is visible; (b) user-reported: 'right, except the flower in the corner' - the shape of the complaint IS the trigger; (c) gross loss it can actually see. On a separable complaint COMPOSITE LEADS and retry follows, because re-rolling to remove a flower re-rolls everything else too. Blocked on MPI-887 (there is no reachable composite to teach) and on the wake-turn question above. Do not build the composite half before 887 lands.

The composite instructions, when they are written, need the app's ON-SCREEN words, the same standing rule that bans saying 'History' to a user. Verified this session: the tool group is Composite, its three buttons are Paint Comp, Mask Comp and Place, the selected entry sits ON TOP and the slot image underneath, and the slot is filled by right-clicking the entry you want underneath -> Send to Composite (MpiToolOptionsComposite.js:16). Read it off the component, never invent the path.

key_decisions: The mask is NOT forced. Fabio, 2026-09-22: 'any edit can be just an edit. It doesn't need to be a localised edit ... The mask is more effective, but shouldn't always be forced on the user.' The fork is one question - does the ask name a PART of the picture - and only the no-preservation-words case is the user's to decide. Do not re-flatten it into 'regional change means mask'.

FILL AND HAND OVER is the answer to run-vs-teach for detail and inpaint, and it came out of Fabio's Flow idea, not out of the original two options. The agent fills what it can, opens the surface, and the user corrects the knobs the agent cannot see before the GPU spends. Neither refuse-and-explain nor run-blind.

Composite is a FIX, not a route to offer up front. Fabio: 'If we're going to do something like that, we might as well offer the mask, not a composite. The composite is something that can be offered after the agent looks at the finished result.' And its trigger must be STRUCTURAL or the user's own complaint, never 'the agent noticed the damage' - auto-look returns a description, not a diff, so a rule gated on spotting a smear silently fails.
A prompt example that was never rendered is not evidence. The one in the system prompt was written down as the prompt the model 'needed' and turned out to be the failure. Render before teaching.

The umbrella exists because Fabio asked for one, so that handoffs keep working a single card. MPI-886 and MPI-887 are named in its plan as related and deliberately NOT members, because a member's description prefix is the only record of membership and writing it means editing cards other sessions own.

Everything else modified in the tree belongs to PEERS - MPI-706, dev_configs/smoke-run.txt, docs/releases/.approved-1.4.2.json, MpiEnhanceDialog.css, resources/cubric/update-manifest.json, the root .agents/mpi-kanban/events.jsonl, and MPI-887's live files (routes/projects.js, MpiMediaPicker.js/.css, MpiPromptBox.js, MpiGroupHistoryBlock.js, tests/project-copy-item.test.cjs). MPI-888's file claims (services/agentLoop.mjs, docs/agent/masking.md, tests/agent-loop.test.cjs) are owned by session 6b5a38e3 and are NOT yours. Any further edit needs fresh claims under the new session id, and a claim record's `path` must be a STRING.

A peer session holds a claim on `.git/`, so the `.git/MSG.txt` commit-message recipe is BLOCKED. Write the message to a dot-file inside the task folder instead (`tasks/MPI-<n>/.commitmsg`), commit with `-F <that path>`, then delete it - it stays untracked and never lands in the commit.

`git commit --only` refuses an UNTRACKED path with 'did not match any file(s) known to git'. Stage new card files with an explicit `git add -- <paths>` first, then commit by pathspec. Never `git add -A`.

Card maturity is `in-progress` with a HYPHEN, not `in_progress` - the validator rejects the underscore and reddens the board. A card in `doing` also needs `checklist.md` to exist, and one in `done` needs `validation.md`.

Closing a card is not enough on its own: the state/tasks/<uuid>.json coordination record must be resolved and removed from index.json active_tasks, or validate_board fails with 'points at done card ... with resolved status in_progress'. Release its file claims in the same pass.
guard-shell blocks heredocs outright, including `python - <<PY`. Write python to a scratchpad file with the Write tool and run it by path.

board.json is CRLF in the repo and LF on write; git normalises it, and the diff stayed at a dozen lines rather than a whole-file re-EOL. Read and write it with io.open(..., newline='') and validate the JSON in memory before writing.
agent-video-attachment.test.cjs prints an AssertionError and is counted by node as `todo`, not `fail`. Pre-existing MPI-867 entry, not a lying pipe.
